Subject: CloudAria partner discovery — next steps & tech deep-dive scheduling

Hi Maya / Tom,

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand CloudAria's marketplace cadence and where a Redwood connector could unlock value for your ISV partners. Quick recap of what we heard on our side:

- Priority use case: reduce inference cost for long-context retrieval apps (vector-index + LLM scoring) across partner tenants.
- Must-haves: per-tenant data isolation, fine-grained routing for low-latency regions, and a predictable SLA for peak-hour batch scoring.
- Questions you raised: support for dedicated pools, KV cache persistence per tenant, and our model rollback/fallback story.

Next steps we recommended on the call:
1) Tech deep-dive (partner-led) with your integration SE and our solutions engineering team to map connector architecture and auth flows.
2) Draft mutual action plan (MAP) to capture milestones and responsibilities.

I can coordinate the deep-dive — proposing 60–75 minute session where we cover architecture, auth (SAML/OIDC), deployment options (hosted vs dedicated), and a quick demo of our routing/fallback policies. Attached is a draft MAP and our 1-pager to speed alignment.

Proposed time windows (PT):
- Tue Dec 8: 10:00–11:15am PT
- Wed Dec 9: 1:00–2:15pm PT

If neither works, please share a couple slots that suit your integration lead. Also helpful to know which CloudAria engineers will join and whether you want a sandbox connector repo ahead of the call.

Thanks — I'll loop in our SE and product owner once we lock a time.

Regards,
Camila Reyes
Partner Lead, Marketplace
Redwood Inference
--

Camila — thanks, great recap.

Tom and I reviewed the notes. We're keen to move to a technical deep-dive next week. A few clarifications from our side before we lock time:

- Our integration lead (Tom) will want to see the auth flow and a short runthrough of your KV cache approach — specifically how you isolate tenant caches and how you handle TTLs on cached prefixes.
- We also want to validate the dedicated-pool scaling model and how auto-fallback behaves when a model is evicted.

Tom is available for the windows you proposed except Dec 9 afternoon. We do have one constraint: our infra team prefers meetings in the 9am–12pm PT block if possible.

We'll plan to have our integration architect (Tom) and one infra engineer on the call. If you can include your SE and someone from product who can speak to rollback policies, that'd be ideal.

Thanks — happy to confirm once you propose a final slot.

—Maya
